newsitem.title: USA: America Online to announce pricing moves.
newsitem.headline: America Online to announce pricing moves.

text.p: America Online Inc., the world's largest online service, is expected to unveil some highly anticipated pricing changes Tuesday, as well as new technologies and directions for the future, analysts said.

America Online, based in Dulles, Va., is expected to unveil a new pricing structure, with possibly three new levels of pricing, including a $19.95 a month for unlimited access, its response to the new pricing of Microsoft Corp., when it relaunched the Microsoft Network a few weeks ago.
"They will do some pricing changes," said Abhishek Gami, an analyst with Nesbitt Burns Securities.
The company is holding a conference call with Wall Street analysts Tuesday morning and a press conference later in New York.
Officials at America Online could not be immediately reached for comment. But an advisory said that the company would make some "pivotal" announcements.

Analysts said the online service, which has been undergoing many changes and pressures in recent months as its subscriber growth has slown, will also discuss some other new pricing points, new technologies and the next version of AOL, code-named Casablanca, targeted for the first quarter of 1997.
